To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the motion of a body in a fluid with a nonstationary potential is described by the Euler–Poincaré equations and that the equilibrium positions are stable when the potential is a minimum of a function of the coordinates.
The stability of equilibrium is investigated for mechanical system in the force field with potential of the type p(t) V.
the stability of the equilibrium positions can be determined by the extremal properties of V, and that the stability conditions are independent of the factor p (t) for large values of t.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following problems: (1) The stability of equilibrium points for a system with a potential function of the form p(t)V. (2) The motion of a rigid solid in an infinite volume filled with an ideal fluid.
the problem of the stability of equilibrium states of mechanical systems under the action of non-stationary external forces.
the stability of the equilibrium positions of mechanical systems in force ﬁelds with potentials of the type p ( t )V, where V is a positive deﬁnite function of the generalized coordi-nates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stability of a system is not affected by a non-stationary potential.
the stability of equilibrium is determined by a comparison of two quantities: one is a function of V and the other is a function of p.

the theory of stability of motion is a very important part of the general theory of dynamical systems, but it is not a separate theory, and it is impossible to develop a general theory of stability without a general theory of dynamically systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have obtained a generalization of Lyapunov’s method of stability analysis for systems with time dependent forces.
in the case of a monotonically increasing p ( t ), the stability conditions for equi-libria are the same as for a constant p ( t ).
the stability of an equilibrium position of a mechanical system in a non-stationary potential field is determined by the same conditions as in a stationary potential field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stability properties of the equilibrium positions in nonstationary force fields can be formulated in terms of extremal properties for the corresponding potential function.
the stability of an equilibrium position of a mechanical system in nonstationary force fields can be reduced to extremal properties of a potential energy function.

if the potential function has the form p (t)V where V is the potential energy function, and the function p (t) is a monotonically increasing function of time, then the equilibrium position of the system is stable if V satisfies certain extremal properties.
